forms.consumer_plugins_hint: Prefer adding authentication under Credentials; the consumer's other plugins go here

forms.global_rules_warning: Global rules run on every request of the gateway.
forms.labels_hint: Key/value pairs to organize and filter resources
forms.no_target: No target: the request must be answered by a plugin (e.g. redirect, mocking, echo).
forms.plugin_config_hint: Reusable set of plugins applied together with this route's
forms.priority_hint: Higher wins when several routes match
forms.private_key_masked: The current key is protected and not shown. To replace it, paste the new key in PEM.
forms.sec_advanced_hint: Labels, timeouts, websocket, vars and other schema fields
forms.service_inherit: The route inherits the service's upstream and plugins; the route's plugins take precedence.
forms.snis_hint: Domains served by this certificate. Accepts *.domain.
forms.token_hint: Prefer a token with a read-only policy
forms.token_masked: Current token masked. Keep it to preserve the value or type a new one.
forms.uris_hint: Use * at the end for a prefix. Enter to add.
forms.username_hint: Letters, digits and _ (cannot be changed later)

set.disabled_plugin_hint: Migrating it disabled uses _meta.disable in APISIX.
set.extra_labels_hint: Added to migrated-from=kong and kong-id, which the migration already writes.
set.host_rewrites_hint: Replaces the host of services and targets, e.g. with the Swarm service name. The Host header sent stays the original one.
set.id_hint: By name the IDs stay readable; by Kong ID they do not change if something is renamed.
set.no_rules: No rules. Plugins without automatic translation show up in the inventory as blocked.
set.prefix_hint: Applied to routes, services, upstreams and global plugins. Consumer usernames do not change.
set.routes_created_hint: When disabled, routes only start serving once enabled at cutover.
set.rules_hint: For custom plugins (or to change the default translation). A rule applies to every occurrence of the plugin: services, routes, consumers and globals.
set.same_id: Object with the same ID in APISIX
set.same_id_hint: Applies to objects that did not come from this migration.
set.saved: The inventory was recalculated with the new defaults.
set.template_help: <field/> copies the value of the Kong plugin keeping its type; <fielddefault/> uses the default when missing; <config/> copies the whole configuration. <plugin/>, <service/>, <route/>, <consumer/> (Kong objects) and <rid/>, <sid/>, <uid/>, <cid/> are also available.
set.template_hint: JSON object generated for each occurrence of the plugin. Fields whose value is missing are omitted.
set.template_not_object: the template must be an object
set.untranslated_hint: Blocking avoids publishing a route without, for example, its authentication.
set.websocket_hint: Kong accepts WebSocket upgrades on any HTTP route; APISIX only with enable_websocket.

note.active_check_unsupported: active health check of type '{type}' is not supported; not migrated
note.add_headers_set: add.headers becomes set: the header is overwritten even if it exists
note.anonymous_missing: anonymous consumer '{consumer}' not found in Kong
note.basic_auth_password: Kong stores only the password hash; set a new password for '{username}' in APISIX
note.basic_auth_reset: passwords do not migrate from Kong (hashed); re-create the basic-auth credentials
note.bot_allow_deny: APISIX does not combine allowlist and denylist; using deny only
note.bot_allow_only: allow-only in Kong whitelists exceptions to the built-in list; in APISIX it becomes an allowlist (blocks everything else)
note.bot_builtin_list: Kong blocks a built-in bot list; APISIX only uses the configured lists
note.cache_content_type: the content_type filter does not exist in APISIX
note.cache_zone: requires the memory_cache zone in apisix.proxy_cache in config.yaml
note.consumer_groups_header: APISIX does not send the X-Consumer-Groups header upstream
note.cors_wildcard_credentials: origin * with credentials: APISIX uses "**", which accepts any origin with credentials
note.expression_routes: expression routes (router expressions) are not supported
note.hash_cookie: cookie hashing: Kong creates cookie '{cookie}' when missing, APISIX does not
note.hash_fallback_unsupported: hash_fallback={value} has no equivalent in APISIX
note.hash_on_unsupported: hash_on={value} has no equivalent; using roundrobin
note.hmac_header: the signature header changes (Kong: hmac username=...; APISIX: Signature keyId=...); clients must adapt
note.host_port_dropped: APISIX does not match the port in the host; '{host}' becomes '{result}'
note.host_rewritten: host rewritten from {from} to {to}; the Host header stays {from_header}
note.http_logger_header: header '{header}' is not supported by http-logger (Authorization only)
note.https_only: HTTPS-only route: HTTP requests get 404 instead of {code}
note.https_redirect_code: the HTTPS redirect uses 301 (GET) or 308 in APISIX instead of {code}
note.id_collision: the generated APISIX ID collides with the one of '{other}'; rename it in Kong or use the Kong ID strategy
note.ip_allow_deny: APISIX does not combine allow and deny; using allow only ({count} deny ranges dropped)
note.jwt_algorithm: algorithm {algorithm} is not supported by APISIX jwt-auth
note.key_also_header: APISIX also accepts the key in the header
note.key_also_query: APISIX also accepts the key in the query string
note.key_collision: the same key-auth key is already in APISIX credential {credential} (credential re-created in Kong?); remove it first
note.key_in_body: key in body (key_in_body) is not supported
note.key_name_single: APISIX accepts a single key name; using '{name}' (of {names})
note.key_ttl: the key expires in Kong (ttl {ttl}s); in APISIX it does not expire
note.limit_by_path: limit_by=path with fixed path '{path}': APISIX limits by each request URI
note.limit_fallback_ip: without an authenticated consumer the limit falls back to the client IP
note.limit_windows: {count} limit windows become limit-count rules (headers prefixed per window)
note.log_format: the APISIX log format differs from Kong; adjust the parser at the destination
note.lua_template: Lua template in '{field}' is not supported; the value is copied as text
note.metrics_names: APISIX metrics have different names (apisix_*); adjust dashboards and alerts
note.oidc_review: Kong Enterprise openid-connect has many options; review the generated configuration
note.passive_check_dropped: APISIX requires an active health check alongside the passive one; the passive health check was not migrated
note.path_handling_v1: path_handling v1: check how the service path is joined with the route path
note.plugin_blocks: the object is blocked so it does not migrate without the plugin
note.plugin_overrides: another Kong plugin also produces {plugin}; this configuration wins
note.policy_cluster: cluster policy (Kong database) does not exist in APISIX; using local (per instance). Consider redis
note.policy_local: local policy: the limit is counted per APISIX instance
note.preflight_continue: preflight_continue has no equivalent (APISIX answers the preflight)
note.preserve_host_mixed: {count} of {total} routes use preserve_host; in APISIX this is set on the upstream (pass_host={pass_host} for all)
note.regex_strip_path: regex path with strip_path: check the generated rewrite (regex_uri)
note.request_buffering: request_buffering=false is not migrated (configure proxy_request_buffering in APISIX)
note.response_buffering: response_buffering=false: use the proxy-buffering plugin if needed
note.rewrite_unsupported_part: {part} of querystring/body is not supported by proxy-rewrite
note.route_no_target: route without a Kong service and without a plugin that answers the request
note.route_service_missing: the route's service {id} does not exist in Kong
note.route_stream_protocol: protocol '{protocol}' uses stream_routes in APISIX; not supported
note.secret_base64: secret_is_base64: in APISIX it is per credential (base64_secret); adjust the jwt-auth credentials
note.service_client_cert: the service uses a client certificate (mTLS) in Kong: set tls.client_cert_id on the upstream
note.service_disabled: service disabled in Kong: its routes will be created disabled
note.service_rewrite_per_route: the service request rewrite (proxy-rewrite) is applied to each route
note.service_stream_protocol: protocol '{protocol}' (TCP/UDP/TLS) uses stream_routes in APISIX; not supported by the migration
note.single_value: {field}: APISIX accepts a single value; using '{value}'
note.snis_ignored: APISIX does not route HTTP by SNI; ignored SNIs: {snis}
note.tcp_logger_sni: tls_sni '{sni}' has no equivalent in tcp-logger
note.trigger_unsupported: trigger '{trigger}' is not supported: the route always answers
note.upstream_client_cert: the upstream uses a client certificate (mTLS) in Kong: set tls.client_cert_id
note.upstream_no_targets: upstream {name} has no targets in Kong
note.upstream_shared: Kong upstream {name} is used by {count} services; each gets its own APISIX upstream (duplicated health checks)
note.username_adjusted: username adjusted to the APISIX format: '{from}' → '{to}'
